angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,435,925 km at 19.21 pc = 1 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 173667: the Hipparcos parallax the radius was computed with (van Leeuwen 2007), 52.06 +/- 0.24 mas, inverted (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101): 19.209 +/- 0.089 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 51.6743 +/- 0.1214 mas (same row, RUWE 2.96), 425.6 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 2.064 +/- 0.017 solar radii from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 173667: radius in solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 1 +/- 0.006 mas (CHARA) and the Hipparcos parallax, 2.064 +/- 0.017 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101): 1,435,925 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.422 +/- 0.009 solar masses from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 173667: mass in solar masses, from Yonsei-Yale isochrones at the measured radius and temperature (a model value), 1.422 +/- 0.009 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6376 +/- 39 K from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 173667: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 6376 +/- 39 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 173667: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 6376 +/- 39 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-173667.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 3.962, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
